prompt: I'd like to see where Ile84 is in 1LMB. Would you draw the protein and DNA as a cartoon and colour Ile84 red?

checks: same reference, accepted alternatives, target, structures, split, tier and family as the original (molbench.tasks.check_corpus)
the reference grades as exactly right against the paraphrase (runner.grade_parsed)
every slot value of the original appears in the wording (nothing needed is dropped)
its twin on the other track has the same words and the same style
provenance.original_prompt: Open 1LMB with the protein and DNA as a cartoon, with Ile84 coloured red.

checks: each of the 3 accepted states: the atoms it draws, read back from pdbe_state.replay, equal the atoms computed from the atom-table columns
reference grades as exactly right against the task (success, F1 1, target score 1; runner.grade_parsed)
every accepted alternative grades as itself, is accepted by the task with target score 1, and is a different final state from the reference
target selects 8 atoms on the frozen atom table
no accepted state equals another (pairwise, by the grader)
twin selects the same target atoms
source.open: which chain's copy of the named residue (or all)
source.rule: The request asks to colour a residue, named by type and author number but with no chain; the protein is present as several identical chains. Accepted: the residue coloured in any one chain, or in every chain.
not_accepted: some but not all chains (when there are more than two): no reading of the request
a residue with that number in another protein of the entry, or the residue with that label (sequence) number where it differs: a different residue
an added representation (sticks) for the residue: only a colour is requested
source.derived: as above, coloured on the cartoon instead of added as sticks. Reference = the first accepted state (ILE 3:84): a bare load, which already draws the polymer as a cartoon and ligands as ball-and-stick, plus one colour call.
source.accepted_differ: accept-set tier: every alternative is another final state, one of the readings of the request that provenance.rule accepts
